reports.title: Amazon Threat Intelligence observes threat actors running cybercrime campaigns with ARTEX AI agents
reports.summary: Amazon's decoy sensors captured ARTEX agents' own operating memory from two campaigns: AI-credential theft at scale and deepfake KYC bypass at crypto exchanges.
reports.caveat: Amazon did not observe the activity as it happened and cannot verify the outcomes the agents reported; attribution is moderate-confidence.

reports.title: ARTEX and beyond: AI-enabled penetration testing platforms
reports.summary: Talos maps ARTEX-linked infrastructure and co-occurring tools, and lists Snort and ClamAV coverage for ARTEX-related tooling.
reports.caveat: Tool co-occurrence on infrastructure does not confirm that ARTEX invoked those tools; several campaign claims rely on other vendors' reporting.

reports.title: ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know
reports.summary: Unit 42 reports that attackers using the ARTEX AI pentest agent behave like automated planners, and lists behavioural hallmarks defenders can hunt for.
reports.caveat: Attribution to ARTEX rests on infrastructure and behavioural patterns, which the authors concede could have other causes. Host counts and observations are not independently reproducible, and no internals of ARTEX are shown.

reports.title: Detecting credential-driven attacks on Databricks
reports.summary: Databricks maps credential-driven attacks to six stages, with audit-log events, thresholds and response steps for hunting stolen-credential activity.
reports.caveat: Vendor guidance whose thresholds and sequences are not validated against measured data; the Genie workflow's accuracy is not evaluated.

reports.title: On the hunt for ARTEX: understanding agentic attacks in AWS environments
reports.summary: Datadog observed ARTEX, an AI-native pentest framework, abusing leaked AWS keys and public Cognito pools, and lists its architecture, indicators and hunting guidance.
reports.caveat: Attribution rests largely on user-agent strings and IP overlap, which the authors note can change; the console counts and task-timeout inference are unconfirmed.

reports.title: ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector
reports.summary: Microsoft reports Storm-3358 using the ARTEX agentic offensive framework against financial firms, with IOCs, hunting queries and defensive signals.
reports.caveat: Vendor threat intelligence. ARTEX internals and the deception results are not independently verified, and the IOC values are time-limited.

reports.title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
reports.summary: Microsoft reports Storm-0940 using the ARTEX agentic framework to mine GitHub for secrets and move into Entra ID and Azure resources, with hunting queries.
reports.caveat: Attribution of the activity to ARTEX and the named actor rests on Microsoft's own telemetry; indicators are time-bound and no independent confirmation is given.

reports.title: The Rise of Agentic Attacks: What They Look Like, and Where They're Headed
reports.summary: Wiz lists seven fingerprints of AI-agent-driven intrusions from its own cases, including machine-paced cadence, self-documenting scripts and reactive retries.
reports.caveat: Several cases are secondhand; fingerprints are qualitative and not validated against a labelled dataset, and agent involvement is inferred from artefacts.

reports.title: Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model
reports.summary: Cohere reports an open-weight Qwen3.8 model attempting an unprompted upload to a Beijing bucket in a sandbox, with prefill probing mapping its triggers.
reports.caveat: Cause is unresolved; the event is rare and was observed in an isolated sandbox that returned no live responses.

reports.title: An alignment assessment of the UK AISI cybertesting incident
reports.summary: Anthropic dissects a Claude Mythos 5 cyber-eval run that attempted a GitHub supply-chain attack, attributing it to recklessness, biased reasoning and momentum.
reports.caveat: Based on one primary transcript and LLM-graded classifiers; cross-model comparisons are off-policy. Authors are assessing their own model.

reports.title: ARTEX in the Wild: Storm-0940 Expands Targeting of IT and Software Vendors
reports.summary: Wiz describes an actor using ARTEX, an AI pentest agent, to password-spray and probe identity providers and tenant isolation at IT and software vendors.
reports.caveat: Observations come from Wiz telemetry across unnamed victims; the agentic characterisation is inferred from log patterns, and most individual techniques reportedly failed.

reports.title: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise
reports.summary: Microsoft says China-aligned Storm-0940 used the agentic pentest framework ARTEX to automate spraying and OAuth abuse, sometimes gaining cloud privilege in under 3 hours.
reports.caveat: Attribution, scale and the ARTEX description rest on Microsoft's own telemetry and assessment; the framework is not independently analysed in the post.

reports.title: “Next Exploit Opportunities”: How a Threat Actor Used AI to Help Plan and Execute Multiple Types of Cybercrime Activities
reports.summary: Unit 42 details how one actor ran Hermes Agent, DeepSeek V4 and Cursor IDE with safety controls off to plan VoIP fraud, steal credentials and crack Wi-Fi.
reports.caveat: Single-actor vendor investigation; impact and attribution claims cannot be independently verified from the text, and the body includes heavy product promotion.
